title: This king spent so much gold its price fell

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1324, one king gave away so much gold its price fell.
beats.visual: Gold coins rain onto a sketched Cairo skyline; a price tag drops

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Mansa Musa ruled Mali, a West African empire rich in gold.
beats.visual: PD Catalan Atlas figure of Mansa Musa slides in; sketch map of the Mali Empire

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Mecca. Accounts describe thousands of followers and 100 camel loads of gold. But there was a problem.
beats.visual: Caravan line crosses the Sahara on the map; camel counter climbs to 100

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Too much generosity. In Cairo, every court official got a load of gold.
beats.visual: PD Bonfils photo of a Cairo mosque gate; gold sacks hop from hand to hand

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Prices fell. Al-Umari, writing in Cairo, says gold stayed cheap about 12 years.
beats.visual: Scale tips: gold coin vs silver coins; calendar flips 12 times

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1375, a European map showed him holding gold. Historians still debate his wealth.
beats.visual: PD Catalan Atlas sheet zooms out; question mark over a money pile

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: One pilgrimage, and gold got cheaper. Follow History Sketches for one wild true story every day.
beats.visual: Coin spins and lands; History Sketches corner logo

description: In 1324 Mansa Musa of Mali passed through Cairo on his way to Mecca and handed out so much gold that, according to the writer al-Umari, its price there stayed low for about twelve years. Narration: synthetic voices. Facts checked against two sources. #history #shorts #africanhistory #mansamusa
title_old: This king was so rich he crashed gold prices
